question.text: An NRI investor redeems equity mutual fund units held for 8 months with a gain of Rs.1,50,000. What is the applicable TDS rate on the capital gain?

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity-oriented mutual fund units held for less than 12 months produce Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG), historically taxed at 15% under Section 111A of the Income Tax Act for the applicable period. For NRI redemptions, TDS is deducted at this STCG rate (plus applicable surcharge and cess). An 8-month holding clearly falls in the STCG window. The Trap: 10% relates to the older equity LTCG rate above the exemption threshold, not STCG. 20% is closer to TDS on IDCW (dividend) for NRIs, not equity STCG. 30% is a generic non-resident slab-style rate that does not apply to equity STCG. Note: The specific 15% STCG rate / Section 111A TDS rate is not stated on the cited Series II-B pages, which describe NRI redemption TDS responsibilities and switch capital-gains treatment at a more general level. The framing above reflects the general Income Tax Act provisions for equity STCG and NRI TDS rather than a direct workbook citation.
